steps.body:
You now have three sign charts and they answer three separate questions:

**f** — above or below the axis?
**f′** — rising or falling?
**f″** — bending up or down?

Stack them and you have the curve. Not an approximation of it — the actual shape, deduced rather than plotted.
The bend chart for a quartic.

widget.prompt: f(x) = x⁴ − 4x³, so f″(x) = 12x(x − 2). Set the sign of f″ on each interval.
widget.successFeedback: + − +. The curve bends UP, then DOWN, then UP — so there are inflection points at both 0 and 2. Now stack this against the f′ chart from chapter 1 (−, −, + with critical points at 0 and 3), and the whole shape appears: falling and concave up, falling and concave down, falling and concave up, then rising. x = 0 is a saddle AND an inflection; x = 3 is the minimum.
widget.crossFeedback: Both roots of f″ are single, so it changes sign at each. Two flips, three intervals.
widget.bounceFeedback: Neither root is repeated here — f″ crosses zero at both 0 and 2 rather than touching.

cml.actionGoal: Set interval signs and use root multiplicity to explain where a function crosses or only touches the axis.

predict.prompt: For f(x) = x⁴ − 4x³ the second derivative f″ = 12x(x − 2) is zero at x = 0 and x = 2. At those two places the curve…

options.label: Reaches a maximum or a minimum

predict.reveal: It changes its bend — these are inflection points. Maxima and minima come from f′, which here is 4x²(x − 3): a different set of places entirely. Three charts, three questions, and reading an answer off the wrong one is the most common way a sketch goes wrong.

explanationVariants: At x = 0, f′ has a double root (so no sign change: a saddle) while f″ has a single root (so a sign change: an inflection). Both statements are true of the same x, and they are about different things.
The charts are independent. A point can be a critical point, an inflection, both, or neither.

widget.prompt: For f = x⁴ − 4x³, x = 0 is a critical point with no sign change in f′, AND a sign change in f″. What is it?

options.label: A saddle AND an inflection point — the two charts describe different things.
options.feedback: Right. f′ says the curve does not turn; f″ says the bend does. Both are true at once, and neither implies the other.

options.label: A minimum.
options.feedback: A minimum needs f′ to change from negative to positive. Here f′ is negative on both sides — the curve is falling through the point.

options.label: Only an inflection — it cannot be a critical point too.
options.feedback: It can, and it is: f′(0) = 0, which is exactly what a critical point means. The two labels are independent.

options.label: Nothing special.
options.feedback: Both derivatives vanish there and one changes sign. That is a great deal of structure for one point.

steps.body:
So sketching is a procedure, not an art:

**Zeros of f** — where it crosses the axis.
**Sign chart of f′** — where it rises and falls; mark the extrema.
**Sign chart of f″** — where it bends; mark the inflections.
**Ends** — what happens as x → ±∞.

Join the dots consistently with all four, and there is only one curve that fits.

explanationVariants: Rising means f′ > 0. Bending downward means f″ < 0. Together: the curve is climbing but levelling off — approaching a peak from the left.
That combination is exactly what the run-up to a maximum looks like.

widget.prompt: On an interval, f′ > 0 and f″ < 0. Which description is guaranteed?

options.label: Rising with a decreasing slope
options.feedback: Right. A positive first derivative means the curve rises, while a negative second derivative means its slope decreases.

options.label: Rising with an increasing slope
options.feedback: That needs f″ > 0 — the slope getting steeper. Here the slope is shrinking.

options.label: Falling with an increasing slope
options.feedback: Falling needs f′ < 0. This curve is going UP; it is just going up more and more gently.

options.label: Constant at a maximum
options.feedback: At the maximum f′ would be 0. It is still positive, so the peak has not arrived yet.

steps.body: Match the pair to the shape.
explanationVariants: Four combinations of two signs, four shapes: rising-concave-up (accelerating climb), rising-concave-down (levelling climb), falling-concave-down (accelerating fall), falling-concave-up (levelling fall).
Every point on every curve is one of these four.

widget.prompt: Match each pair of signs to what the curve is doing.

pairErrors.feedback: f″ < 0 means the slope is SHRINKING, so the climb is easing off rather than steepening.
f′ < 0 means the curve is going DOWN, not climbing.

widget.missFeedback: The sign of f′ says up or down. The sign of f″ says whether that is intensifying or easing.
widget.successFeedback: Direction from f′, and whether it is intensifying from f″. Four combinations, and every point on every curve is one of them.

hints: f′ = 3x² − 12x = 3x(x − 4), so the critical points are 0 and 4.
f″ = 6x − 12 = 6(x − 2), so the single inflection is at x = 2.
The question asks how many inflection points there are — not critical points.
explanationVariants: f″ = 6(x − 2) has one single root, so it changes sign once: exactly ONE inflection point, at x = 2.
The two critical points (0 and 4) are a different question, answered by a different chart.

widget.prompt: f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 5. How many inflection points does it have?

commonErrors.feedback: Two is the number of CRITICAL points (0 and 4). Inflections come from f″ = 6x − 12, which has a single root at x = 2.
f″ = 6x − 12 does change sign — negative for x < 2 and positive after. That is one inflection.
A linear f″ can change sign at most once.

widget.fallbackFeedback: f″ = 6(x − 2): one root, one sign change, one inflection point.

takeaways: f says where the curve sits, f′ says which way it goes, f″ says how it bends. Three questions, three charts.
A single x can be a critical point AND an inflection — the labels are independent.
Sketching is deduction, not plotting: only one curve is consistent with all three charts.
steps.teaser: Still to come in this course: the Mean Value Theorem, curve sketching in full, and optimisation.

concept.body: Two independent questions at every point. **Which way am I going?** — the sign of f′. **Is that intensifying or easing?** — the sign of f″. Four combinations, and every point on every curve is one of them.

explanationVariants: f′ < 0 and f″ > 0: falling, but the fall is easing off — approaching a minimum.
Negative slope, increasing slope: the descent is flattening out.

widget.prompt: f′ < 0 and f″ > 0. What is the curve doing?

options.label: Falling, but the fall is easing off.
options.feedback: Right — a negative slope that is rising toward zero. The run-up to a minimum.

options.label: Falling faster and faster.
options.feedback: That is f″ < 0. A positive f″ means the slope is INCREASING — heading back toward zero.
